name: WEP FMS attack
flag_signature: the recovered WEP key is the flag or immediately decrypts a target frame
notes: Historical; superseded by PTW for speed, but the FMS bias exists on any WEP AP.

name: WEP KoreK attack
notes: 17 statistical biases extending FMS.

name: WEP PTW attack
notes: aircrack-ng's default WEP attack. Sub-minute recovery when ARP-request replay accelerates IV generation.

name: WEP ARP-request replay (traffic accelerator)
preconditions: at least one seen ARP request
notes: Replaying a captured ARP request generates fresh encrypted responses at line rate, feeding FMS/KoreK/PTW.

name: TKIP Beck-Tews MIC key recovery
target_availability_2026: rare — TKIP effectively extinct on modern infrastructure
notes: Record exists, technique works where TKIP survives (legacy WPA1). Rarely reached for.

name: WPA2 4-way handshake capture
flag_signature: PSK is the flag OR PSK decrypts a target frame containing the flag
notes: The DEFCON WCTF workhorse. Minimal handshake for hashcat is M1+M2 (or M2+M3); older cracks needed the full 4-way.

name: PMKID capture attack
preconditions: target uses WPA2-PSK or WPA3-transition WPA2 side
target AP includes PMKID in first EAPOL / RSN IE
mitigation: AP firmware omits PMKID from M1
flag_signature: PSK is the flag
notes: Faster than 4-way capture — no client needed. Vendor adoption of the mitigation is uneven; many consumer APs in 2026 still leak PMKID.

name: WPS PIN online brute (Reaver)
flag_signature: PSK recovered via WPS is the flag
notes: Vendor lockout and Wi-Fi Alliance's WPS deprecation guidance have thinned the target pool; still viable on ISP-supplied routers.

name: WPS Pixie Dust offline attack
notes: Offline recovery of the WPS PIN from E-S1/E-S2; not every chipset is vulnerable.

name: WPS null-PIN attack
preconditions: WPS registrar accepts empty PIN (vendor-specific bug)
notes: Rare, but persistent on specific vendor generations.

name: WPS vendor-derivable PIN (MAC/OUI-derived)
preconditions: target vendor derives PIN from MAC (Belkin, D-Link, some TP-Link generations)
notes: First-try success on affected vendors; use vendor+chipset lookup to decide.

name: KRACK — client-side pairwise key reinstall (M3 replay)
preconditions: multi-channel MitM between client and legitimate AP
flag_signature: decrypted client traffic contains the flag; on some Linux clients the PTK is reinstalled to all-zero → trivial decrypt

name: KRACK — Linux/Android wpa_supplicant all-zero PTK reinstall
notes: Extreme version of KRACK — PTK is reinstalled to all-zero, decryption is trivial.

name: Dragonblood — SAE cache-based side channel
preconditions: co-located attack surface (adjacent process on same host, or timing over LAN)

name: WPA3 transition-mode downgrade to WPA2
preconditions: AP RSN IE carries AKM 2 (PSK) AND AKM 8 (SAE)
flag_signature: PSK recovered from the WPA2-side handshake

name: Kr00k (Broadcom/Cypress) — all-zero PTK on disassoc
preconditions: target client uses vulnerable Broadcom/Cypress chipset
flag_signature: post-disassoc tail frames decrypt with the zero key; typically a few TCP/UDP payload bytes
target_availability_2026: flagship phones patched; older Echo/Kindle/WiFi cameras still vulnerable

name: FragAttacks — A-MSDU flag confusion plaintext injection
preconditions: client that accepts non-SPP A-MSDU frames

name: FragAttacks — mixed-key fragment cache
preconditions: client stores fragments across rekey boundary

name: SSID Confusion — 4-way handshake does not authenticate SSID
preconditions: client trusts SSID for policy decisions (VPN auto-connect, trust-on-SSID)
tools: custom hostapd fork advertising the target SSID over a different network
mitigation: SSID authentication in the 4-way (patched clients on some OSes as of 2026)
flag_signature: client sends VPN-off or trust-on-SSID traffic under the belief it's on network X

name: Framing Frames — power-save queue poisoning (Vanhoef 2023)
preconditions: target client honors PM bit; AP queues frames on sleep
flag_signature: attacker-injected frame is delivered to a client whose isolation would otherwise have blocked it

name: MacStealer — MAC-based traffic hijack (Vanhoef 2023)
preconditions: attacker on same network; client MAC known

name: Wi-Fi 7 MLO link-desync primitive
preconditions: attacker can suppress or desync one of the links
notes: Frontier research; expect published PoCs at DEF CON 33 / 34.

name: 802.11r FT-handshake capture
flag_signature: recovered PSK from the FT reassoc

name: BTM (802.11v) forced roam onto rogue BSSID
preconditions: attacker in RF range and channel
notes: Crafted BTM Request from a rogue shoves the client onto the attacker BSSID with the client's cooperation. PMF does not protect BTM Action frames as of 802.11-2020 §11.24 for all vendors.

name: 802.11k Neighbor Report spoof
notes: Steer the target into associating with your BSSID by naming it as a preferred neighbor.

name: ANQP Realm / Roaming-Consortium enumeration (pre-association)
preconditions: target AP is Interworking / Passpoint capable
flag_signature: flag embedded in a Passpoint OSU / NAI Realm / Venue Info element

name: Multi-Channel MitM (dual-radio)
preconditions: victim on channel A; attacker AP on channel B; interpose
notes: Underlies KRACK. Useful standalone in modern evil-twin work when band-steering / 11k/11v steer clients across bands.

name: Broadcast deauth flood
preconditions: target AP or client with PMF-disabled
flag_signature: target client re-associates; capture the resulting 4-way
caveat: Transmitting. Only fire with airspace authorization.

name: Targeted deauth (unicast)
caveat: Transmitting. Only fire with airspace authorization.

name: Beacon flood (mdk4 mode b)
flag_signature: confusion / decoy — some CTF scoring bots use beacon count as a signal

name: TKIP Michael MIC failure DoS
flag_signature: some WCTF puzzles use 'seen a Michael MIC failure' as a flag trigger

name: Evil-twin — clone SSID+BSSID+channel of a target AP
tools: aireplay-ng -0 (to knock clients off legit AP)
mitigation: client-side AP authentication (WPA2-Enterprise cert pinning, WPA3-SAE with unique password per network)
flag_signature: victim client connects to your BSSID; capture its traffic or serve a captive portal

name: MANA — per-STA SSID-pool probe response (SensePost 2014)
flag_signature: client associates to a rogue AP believing it's on a preferred network

name: MANA Loud — broadcast union of all seen probes
MANA Known Beacons — dictionary-broadcast SSID pool
Captive-portal credential capture
flag_signature: flag is whatever the user types in the login form (WCTF classic)

name: Rogue RADIUS — hostapd-wpe inner-EAP capture
preconditions: victim client with weak cert validation
flag_signature: MSCHAPv2 challenge-response captured → hashcat 5500 / asleap → password

name: Rogue RADIUS — eaphammer end-to-end
preconditions: victim client with weak cert validation
flag_signature: inner MSCHAPv2 or GTC captured under a rogue tunnel

name: Cert-phishing — weak client cert validation
preconditions: victim's WPA-Enterprise profile does not pin the RADIUS server certificate

name: EAP inner-method downgrade — PEAP → GTC (plaintext token)
flag_signature: plaintext OTP (RSA / Duo / Yubico) captured within its validity window

name: LEAP legacy offline crack (asleap)
target_availability_2026: rare — LEAP mostly extinct; some legacy WLCs still surface

name: Default-PSK derivation — UPC/UBEE
flag_signature: PSK derived from SSID — validate against a captured PMKID or handshake
notes: No radio time required. Common WCTF sleeper puzzle.

name: Default-PSK derivation — Thomson Speedtouch (SSID suffix hash)
preconditions: target SSID matches SpeedTouch prefix + 6-digit hash

name: PineAP passive probe log
flag_signature: target's preferred-network SSID leaks in its probe request

name: PineAP active karma (probe-response to any request)
caveat: Transmitting probe responses to real clients; needs airspace authorization.

name: PineAP SSID-pool broadcast (known-beacons style)
tools: PineAP module → SSID Pool → Broadcast SSID pool

name: RNR-driven 6 GHz enumeration from 2.4/5 GHz beacons
preconditions: target advertises RNR in 2.4/5 GHz beacons
flag_signature: 6 GHz BSSID recovered without a 6 GHz-capable radio

name: Arbitrary 802.11 frame injection
caveat: Transmitting. Only fire with airspace authorization.

name: Beacon-IE stego (Vendor-Specific payload)
flag_signature: flag concatenated in a custom OUI Vendor-Specific IE across many beacons

name: WPS negative-PIN / EAP-WSC state machine bugs
preconditions: chipset-specific state machine bug where negative or malformed PIN values are accepted
tools: reaver with a custom PIN value; oneshotpin fork
notes: Rare but persistent on specific vendor firmware generations. Combine with vendor + Manufacturer IE probe first.

name: WPS-Locked bypass via timing (lock reset)
preconditions: target enters WPS-Locked state after N failures
lockout duration is finite and predictable
notes: Most consumer AP firmware resets WPS-Locked after 60–300 s. Wait, resume.

name: WPS PBC (push-button) 2-minute window abuse
preconditions: target user just pressed the WPS push-button
attacker in RF range during the 2-minute window
flag_signature: PSK returned when the attacker enrolls as any Enrollee during the open window
notes: Requires social-engineering the button press or a very lucky observation.

name: KRACK — WNM Sleep Mode key reinstall
preconditions: client that supports 802.11v WNM Sleep Mode

name: FragAttacks — fragmentation cache not cleared on connect
preconditions: client stack retains fragmentation cache across (re)connect

name: SAE H2E follow-up side channel
preconditions: H2E implementation with residual timing leakage under specific conditions
notes: H2E mitigates the 2019 hunt-and-peck timing oracle; some 2021+ implementations still leak under narrower conditions.

name: Dragonblood — MODP-group downgrade
preconditions: rogue AP advertises only a weak MODP group in SAE Group Negotiation
tools: custom hostapd with MODP-only group list
mitigation: disable MODP groups in hostapd_cli; enforce ECC-only

name: FT PMK-R0 shared-fleet crack (misconfig)
preconditions: misconfigured 11r deployment that shares PMK-R0 across all BSSIDs in the Mobility Domain
flag_signature: one recovered PSK unlocks every BSSID in the mobility domain
notes: The catastrophic 11r failure mode.

name: EAP-GTC plaintext token capture
preconditions: client tolerates PEAP → GTC inner-method downgrade
target uses OTP-style GTC token (RSA / Duo / Yubico)
flag_signature: plaintext OTP captured inside the rogue PEAP tunnel; usable within its validity window (typically 30–60 s)

name: MDM device-profile theft via captive portal
preconditions: victim's enterprise WiFi profile can be reinstalled from a captive portal
captive portal serves a fake MDM enrollment page
tools: custom captive portal + apple/msi profile mime types
flag_signature: victim installs a rogue MDM profile that swaps their RADIUS trust anchor

name: MSCHAPv2 challenge/response capture (outer or inner)
preconditions: captured MSCHAPv2 exchange from rogue-RADIUS or inner-EAP downgrade

name: Default-PSK derivation — Netgear Genie
preconditions: AP is a Netgear from the 2011–2020 Genie firmware generation

name: CSA spoof to drag client to rogue channel
notes: Modern clients require CSA to appear inside a protected mgmt frame or ignore it.

name: WNM Sleep Mode key reinstall / abuse
TDLS teardown injection
preconditions: two clients set up a TDLS direct link
notes: Break the TDLS peer link with an injected teardown; forces STA-to-STA traffic back through the AP where it can be observed.

name: Malformed / oversized IE beacon crash
preconditions: victim client with vulnerable driver / firmware parses attacker-crafted oversized Vendor-Specific IE
notes: Not gone. Some cheap consumer client stacks still OOM.

name: EAPOL 4-way nonce reuse observation
preconditions: passive observation of a KRACK-triggered nonce reuse
notes: Diagnostic — detect whether a KRACK attempt fired successfully by looking for reused PN values on the AP-to-STA data stream.

name: Band-steering coercion via 5-GHz suppression
preconditions: AP fleet uses band-steering to prefer 5 GHz; attacker jams or spoofs congestion on 5 GHz
tools: mdk4 v (NAV) on 5 GHz + rogue 2.4 GHz AP
notes: Companion to MC-MitM — drives clients to the band you control.

name: KRACK — Broadcast GTK replay against unpatched clients
preconditions: unpatched client + attacker replays the group-key handshake message
